[Robinson et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.04592) study controllable hardness; [Wang and Liu](https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2021/html/Wang_Understanding_the_Behaviour_of_Contrastive_Loss_CVPR_2021_paper.html) analyze temperature-dependent hardness penalties.

Proposed controlled ablations: baseline; mass-preserving hardness weighting, rescaling weights so Σwᵢexp(sᵢ)=Σexp(sᵢ); pressure-only weighting, assigning every negative the same multiplier matching the weighted method’s per-example M; and the full method. Detach normalization factors consistently, otherwise exact mass preservation can cancel the intended reweighting gradient. Compare constant, delayed, ramped and reversed schedules with matched cumulative pressure; include detached versus differentiable weights and fixed versus learned score scale. Hold candidates, seeds and training budget fixed. Track M/exp(s₊), positive-gradient magnitude, negative-gradient concentration, score norms and macro validation HR@10. Evidence supports a risk, not a universal indictment of hardness weighting. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) documents false-negative problems in sequential recommendation and reports improvements from handling suspected false negatives across three backbones. [AHNS](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709/29371), studying collaborative filtering, explains how consistently selecting hard negatives can suppress relevant but unobserved items. Self-adversarial weighting plausibly magnifies this problem by assigning larger penalties to high-scoring candidates; that mechanism is an inference, not direct evidence for this BERT4Rec configuration.

Popularity effects depend on the sampler and dataset. A [20-repeat sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/html/2410.17276v2) found adaptive mixed sampling improved overall accuracy while retaining strong head–tail imbalance on Amazon Beauty; uniform sampling itself reinforced popularity bias. Hardness therefore need not increase popularity bias relative to uniform, and aggregate HR@10 cannot establish whether it does.

Suggested history-only diagnostics: log negative weight mass by training-frequency decile, score–log-frequency correlation, weight entropy and effective sample size, 1/Σw² for normalized weights; measure recommendation head share, catalog coverage and exposure Gini. Compare recommendation popularity with each user’s historical popularity profile. For false-negative risk, audit collisions with known training positives, including other masked targets, and measure weighted overlap with later observed interactions inside training histories using retrospective prefix probes. Report overlap rates and assigned weight mass relative to uniform sampling. Historical co-occurrence similarity offers another suspicion proxy, not a label.
